text: A microscopic pedestrian simulation reproduced crowd densities on the redesigned square using calibrated behavioural parameters and no field instrumentation.
label: Not related

text: Inertial sensors on shared e-bikes characterised road surface vibration along cycling corridors.
label: Not related

text: A wearable system recorded joint kinematics of participants walking on an instrumented laboratory walkway during a clinical assessment.
label: Not related

text: Handheld thermal and illuminance instruments recorded conditions at pedestrian height beneath arcades and in adjacent open sections of the same street.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: A pedestrian-borne camera and GNSS rig captured continuous footway imagery from which surface defects and vertical displacements were automatically detected.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Deep learning estimation of building height from aerial imagery. Accurate building height data support a range of urban analyses. This work trains a network to regress building height from high-resolution aerial imagery combined with shadow information, evaluated against airborne lidar-derived reference heights. Performance was assessed across building typologies and densities. Errors were largest for low-rise structures in dense blocks, and the derived height layer was released for the study region.
label: Not related

text: Ground-level radiometric measurement of shade quality along pedestrian arcades. Not all shade is equally effective, since reflected and emitted radiation from surrounding surfaces continues to load pedestrians. Net radiometers and globe thermometers were deployed at pedestrian height beneath arcades, tree canopies and fabric canopies along the same street. Mean radiant temperature was computed for each shading type across clear summer days. Tree canopies outperformed built shading of equivalent geometric coverage, and the differential was attributed to lower surface temperatures of vegetated surfaces.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Text mining of planning documents for references to active travel. Policy language shapes implementation. This study applies natural language processing to a corpus of local planning documents to identify and classify references to walking and cycling provision over two decades. Frequency and framing were compared across jurisdictions and periods. References increased substantially while specific commitments remained rare, and no environmental data were collected.
label: Not related

text: GPS-defined activity spaces and dietary behaviour in mid-life adults. Smartphone GPS traces delineated activity spaces, which were linked to commercial listings and census characteristics. Daily mobility may expose individuals to food environments beyond their residential neighbourhood. Dietary intake was collected through ecological momentary surveys and analysed against environmental exposure. Food purchases were more strongly associated with outlets encountered near workplaces than with those around the residential address.
label: Not related

text: Wearable step counts before and after a walking-promotion campaign. A municipal campaign encouraged residents to increase daily walking through goal setting and social challenges. To address this, consumer activity trackers supplied step counts for intervention and comparison groups over sixteen weeks. Changes in activity and programme engagement were estimated with mixed models. Step counts increased during the first month but returned close to baseline after the social challenge ended.
label: Not related

text: Portable structured-light audit of platform-to-street pedestrian transitions. A handheld structured-light scanner captured stairs, ramps, tactile surfaces and threshold gaps along transfer paths at 34 stations. Geometric attributes were compared with accessibility standards and verified by repeat scans. Connections between transit platforms and surrounding streets contain small level changes that conventional accessibility databases overlook. Most failures occurred at interfaces managed by different agencies rather than within the station buildings themselves.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Pedometer-assessed walking across neighbourhood income groups. The study compared daily walking behaviour among residents of areas with different socioeconomic profiles. Methodologically, participants recorded pedometer totals and completed questionnaires about perceived safety and access to destinations. Area classifications were taken from census data and municipal statistics. Daily step totals differed by neighbourhood income, although the association weakened after adjustment for age and employment.
label: Not related

text: Perceived sidewalk quality from a resident telephone survey. Residents were asked whether neighbourhood streets supported comfortable walking. To address this, a structured telephone survey collected ratings of sidewalk condition, lighting, traffic and aesthetics, alongside reported walking frequency. Responses were aggregated by district and compared with demographic characteristics. Perceived maintenance and traffic safety were the strongest correlates of reported neighbourhood walking.
label: Not related

text: Expert panel evaluation of rendered complete-street alternatives. The study explored professional preferences for alternative street designs. In the reported study, architects and transport planners viewed computer-rendered cross-sections varying in tree planting, lane allocation and sidewalk width, then scored walkability and feasibility. Experts preferred designs with wider sidewalks and protected crossings but disagreed about the amount of on-street parking to retain. Consensus and disagreement were analysed across disciplines.
label: Not related

text: Street imagery assessment of crossing visibility under seasonal vegetation. Sight lines at crossings can deteriorate as foliage develops even when fixed infrastructure remains unchanged. To address this, panoramic images acquired in leaf-off and leaf-on seasons were used to reconstruct the pedestrian-driver visibility envelope and identify vegetation intrusions. On-site distance measurements confirmed the model at a sample of crossings. Seasonal loss of visibility was concentrated at suburban junctions where private hedges bordered the waiting area.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Virtual reality exposure to streetscape greenery and stress. A laboratory experiment tested whether simulated greenery affected psychological response. To address this, participants viewed computer-generated street scenes in a headset while heart rate and skin conductance were recorded. Scene variables were experimentally controlled and no real locations were surveyed. Scenes with more vegetation reduced self-reported stress, while physiological effects varied considerably between participants.
label: Not related

text: Acoustic detection of audible pedestrian signals at urban intersections. Audible crossing cues are essential for many visually impaired pedestrians but are not reliably documented. In the reported study, directional microphones recorded signal cycles at intersections, and an audio classifier distinguished locator tones, walk indications and surrounding traffic noise. The sensing campaign identified units that were installed but functionally inaudible during peak traffic conditions. Technicians verified device presence and operating status during field visits.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Solar geometry model for future sidewalk shade planning. Planners estimated how proposed buildings would affect route-level shade. Building massing models and solar position algorithms generated hourly shadow maps for design alternatives. The results supported planning review but were not validated with pedestrian-height measurements. Proposed massing alternatives differed greatly in afternoon shade despite similar total building floor area.
label: Not related

text: Lidar-based sidewalk recognition for autonomous delivery robots. A navigation system enabled a robot to distinguish sidewalks, kerbs and obstacles in real time. In the reported study, onboard lidar and cameras fed a perception stack that produced traversability labels and collision-free local paths. The perception stack improved mission completion and reduced emergency stops in cluttered sidewalk scenes. Performance was evaluated through autonomous missions.
label: Not related

text: Pedestrian-level turbulence sensing near building corner entrances. Strong, rapidly fluctuating winds at building corners can make entrances difficult to approach on foot. In the reported study, three-dimensional ultrasonic anemometers recorded at pedestrian height around tower entrances, while short video samples documented hesitation and route deviation. The highest turbulence occurred outside the zones predicted from mean wind speed alone. Measurements were grouped by upstream wind direction and compared with design comfort criteria.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Sidewalk map alignment for an autonomous campus shuttle. The study improved map matching for a small robotic vehicle operating on shared paths. In the reported study, gNSS, inertial and lidar data were fused to localise the shuttle relative to a high-definition map. Map alignment reduced lateral localisation error and improved completion of long campus routes. Evaluation reported trajectory error and mission completion.
label: Not related

text: Street imagery and retail sales forecasting for commercial corridors. Panoramic images were processed to extract storefront visibility, signage density, facade condition and apparent pedestrian presence, then combined with anonymised transaction totals in gradient-boosting models. Visual indicators improved prediction for restaurants and convenience stores. The target was commercial performance, and the study did not evaluate whether the streets were accessible, comfortable or otherwise walkable.
label: Not related

text: Roadside camera estimation of vehicle emissions at signalised junctions. Video analytics classified vehicle type, queue length and acceleration events, and these outputs were entered into an emissions model to estimate hourly nitrogen oxide and carbon dioxide production. Estimates were checked against short roadside sampling campaigns. The project focused on traffic emissions management and did not characterise pedestrian exposure or walking-environment quality.
label: Not related

text: Mobile mapping inventory of drinking fountains along hot-weather routes. Access to drinking water can influence the practicality of longer walks during heat. To address this, street imagery and range data were processed to locate fountains, measure approach clearance and determine whether controls were reachable from a wheelchair. Operational status was checked during two summer visits. Only half of mapped fountains were both functional and accessibly approached, creating long service gaps on several popular routes.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Airborne lidar inventory of urban canopy volume. A national mapping programme quantified vegetation structure across metropolitan regions. To address this, airborne point clouds were classified to estimate canopy height, volume and change by administrative area. Field plots supported accuracy assessment. Canopy volume increased in outer districts but declined along several intensively redeveloped corridors.
label: Not related

text: Seasonal monitoring of leaf litter and drainage obstruction on footways. Autumn leaf accumulation can conceal defects and increase slip risk on pedestrian routes. Repeated downward imagery, moisture sensing and drainage observations were collected after rainfall along tree-lined streets. A classifier mapped leaf coverage and blocked inlets, while friction tests validated risk categories. Hazard duration depended more on drainage condition and maintenance timing than on total canopy density.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Integrating complaint records with sensed sidewalk defects to identify reporting bias. Mobile imagery and inertial roughness sensing produced an independent defect inventory that was compared with geocoded complaints over the same period. Municipal complaint systems may underrepresent barriers in areas where residents report less frequently. Defects were matched by type, severity and location. Complaint coverage varied strongly by neighbourhood even after controlling for measured defect density, revealing where proactive inspection was most necessary.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Ambient light and pedestrian presence sensing in park connector paths. Low-use park links can remain dark because lighting operation is scheduled without evidence of actual pedestrian demand. In the reported study, illuminance sensors and anonymous thermal counters monitored connector paths across seasons, measuring delivered light and pedestrian presence by time of night. Several routes experienced regular use after lighting was dimmed, while other brightly lit periods had almost no pedestrian activity. Data were compared with programmed luminaire schedules.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Wearable physiology during occupational construction work. Sensors quantified physical strain across construction tasks. Methodologically, workers wore heart-rate and inertial devices during shifts, with observers annotating task categories. Results informed rotation schedules. Several construction tasks exceeded recommended strain thresholds and were prioritised for rotation.
label: Not related

text: Network-based walkability score from open spatial data. Intersection density, destination access, residential density and slope from a digital elevation model were standardised and weighted. Scores were compared with an existing index. A new index estimated walkability at road-network nodes rather than administrative areas. The method relied on conventional geospatial datasets and did not sense street-level pedestrian conditions.
label: Not related

text: Ultrasonic and optical sensing for continuous monitoring of footway obstruction in a historic centre. Temporary obstructions such as café terraces, delivery pallets and construction hoardings intermittently reduce walking space but are invisible to static inventories. A network of low-power ultrasonic and optical units was installed along a heritage street to detect lateral encroachment onto the footway at fifteen-minute intervals over six months. Detected obstruction width was validated against periodic manual measurement. Encroachment exceeded one metre during 19 percent of daytime hours, concentrated in the late afternoon.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Association between neighbourhood environment perceptions and self-reported walking in older adults. Perceived environment is an established correlate of walking behaviour. This cross-sectional survey administered a validated neighbourhood environment scale together with a physical activity questionnaire to community-dwelling older adults. Associations between perceived attributes and reported walking for transport and recreation were estimated with regression models adjusting for demographic characteristics. Perceived safety from traffic and access to destinations were most strongly associated with transport walking.
label: Not related

text: Traffic sign detection and inventory from vehicle-mounted imagery. Maintaining accurate signage inventories is a costly obligation for road authorities. This work presents a detection and classification pipeline applied to imagery collected from a survey vehicle, identifying regulatory, warning and informational signs and assessing their retroreflectivity condition. Performance was evaluated on a manually annotated benchmark. The system supports automated updating of asset registers and identification of signs requiring replacement.
label: Not related

text: Crowd density estimation for event safety management using overhead cameras. Managing large gatherings requires real-time awareness of crowd conditions. Overhead cameras coupled with a density estimation network were deployed at a stadium concourse to produce continuous occupancy estimates. The system was validated against manual counts during three events. Alert thresholds were derived from published crowd safety guidance and integrated into the venue operations dashboard.
label: Not related

text: Automated recognition of pedestrian wayfinding signage from street-level imagery. Legible wayfinding supports independent walking, particularly for visitors and people with cognitive impairment. Street-level images were processed with a detection and text recognition pipeline to locate and read pedestrian wayfinding signs, mapping their density and continuity along principal routes. Detection performance was validated on site. Signage continuity broke down at district boundaries, where responsibility for provision was divided between authorities.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Pedestrian-height wind and turbulence measurement around tall building podiums. Podium design influences ground-level wind conditions. Ultrasonic anemometers were installed at pedestrian height around three tall building podiums of differing geometry and recorded for twelve months. Gust equivalent mean speeds were computed and classified against comfort and safety criteria. Podium setback and canopy presence were associated with measurable reductions in exceedance frequency, and measurements were compared with wind tunnel predictions for the same sites.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Combining segmented imagery and portable sensing to profile school walking routes. Routes used by children merit specific assessment. A rig combining a chest camera, particulate sensor and sound level meter was carried along designated school routes, and imagery was segmented to record footway presence, width and crossing provision. Environmental channels supplied continuous exposure profiles. Routes with the highest measured pollutant and noise exposure were not those identified as hazardous by the existing school travel plan.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Ground-level imaging of vegetation condition along pedestrian corridors. Vegetation contributes to comfort and pleasantness only when it is healthy and appropriately maintained. Street-level images captured across two growing seasons were processed to estimate canopy density, foliage condition and pruning-induced asymmetry along pedestrian corridors. Automated estimates were compared with arborist assessment on a sample. Corridors with recurrent utility pruning showed persistently reduced canopy on the footway side, translating into measurably reduced shade at pedestrian level.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Acoustic monitoring of bird communities in urban parks. Urban biodiversity monitoring benefits from automated methods. Autonomous recording units deployed across urban parks captured dawn chorus recordings over a breeding season, and species were identified with an acoustic classification model validated against expert annotation. Species richness was related to park size, vegetation structure and surrounding built density. Larger parks with structurally complex vegetation supported higher richness.
label: Not related

text: Neighbourhood walkability index and hypertension incidence in a national cohort. Built environment may influence cardiovascular risk through long-term activity patterns. The study therefore used the following approach: residential addresses were linked to an established index combining density, land-use mix and intersection connectivity, while incident hypertension was obtained from administrative health records. Higher index values were associated with lower risk after adjustment for income and baseline health, but no environmental sensing or street-level measurement was conducted. The study evaluates health associations of a precomputed walkability measure.
label: Not related

text: Structured-light assessment of tactile warning surfaces at rail-station approaches. Tactile paving must retain a recognisable profile and continuous alignment to provide reliable guidance. The study therefore used the following approach: handheld structured-light scans were collected at station entrances, platform approaches and adjoining crossings, and rib height, spacing and directional continuity were extracted. Worn or misaligned surfaces were concentrated at recently resurfaced interfaces and were confirmed by accessibility auditors. The method enables repeatable monitoring of a feature usually recorded only as present or absent.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: School-neighbourhood walkability and children's independent mobility. Parents completed travel and independence questionnaires, while school-area walkability was computed from land-use and network datasets. Intersection density and destination access were positively associated with independent trips. These observations are important because environmental context may influence whether children travel without adult accompaniment. The study does not instrument or directly measure the walking environment.
label: Not related

text: Walk Score and retail vacancy in suburban centres. Commercial vitality may be related to pedestrian accessibility. Publicly available Walk Score values were linked to business-register data and property records for suburban centres. Higher scores were associated with lower vacancy after controlling for regional demand. The analysis relies on a proprietary composite score and does not sense pedestrian-scale conditions.
label: Not related

text: Accessibility to parks and self-reported recreational walking. Network distance to parks was calculated from municipal GIS layers and compared with recreational walking reported in telephone interviews. This design responds to the fact that proximity to green space is frequently proposed as a walking support. Closer proximity predicted more frequent walking only among respondents with dogs. No sensor-based characterisation of route quality or pedestrian conditions was undertaken.
label: Not related

text: Ground-camera reconstruction of sidewalk edge drop-offs. Downward-facing cameras and inertial sensing captured edge geometry along narrow residential streets, and a model estimated drop height, lateral clearance and presence of guarding. Field checks confirmed reliable detection of hazardous sections, particularly where vegetation obscured the edge. These observations are important because unprotected edge drops create fall risk where footways run beside drainage channels or retaining walls. The approach extends walkability assessment to a rarely inventoried safety condition.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Development of a rural walkability index from open data. Most walkability measures have been designed for dense urban settings. The study therefore used the following approach: road connectivity, population distribution, services and slope were combined from open geospatial datasets and weighted through expert judgement. The resulting score differentiated village centres from dispersed settlements. The contribution is a GIS index rather than sensing of physical walking environments.
label: Not related

text: Lidar-based localisation of a service robot on pedestrian paths. Reliable localisation is challenging where GNSS signals are obstructed. The proposed workflow combined field acquisition and analysis: robot-mounted lidar scans were matched to a prebuilt map using a probabilistic registration method. Localisation error remained below the navigation tolerance across an outdoor campus route. The sensing supports robot pose estimation and does not inventory the pedestrian environment.
label: Not related

text: Automated timing audit of pedestrian signals using computer vision. Published signal plans do not always reflect the timing experienced by pedestrians. The proposed workflow combined field acquisition and analysis: video recordings at signalised intersections were analysed to detect pedestrian indications, countdown displays and actual crossing trajectories. Measured clearance frequently differed from controller records, and slower walkers were disproportionately exposed at wide intersections. The workflow supports empirical evaluation of crossing adequacy.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Thermal-camera observation of pedestrian yielding after dark. Conventional video can undercount pedestrians in poorly illuminated environments. In the empirical work, thermal cameras recorded crossing attempts and driver yielding at unsignalised sites over winter evenings, with trajectories extracted automatically. Yielding probability declined with vehicle speed and when pedestrians waited beyond the main beam of street lighting. The sensor choice enabled reliable behavioural measurement under conditions relevant to night-time walkability.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Computer vision inventory of facade materials for energy modelling. Building-energy analysis requires information on envelope construction. The proposed workflow combined field acquisition and analysis: street images were classified into masonry, concrete, glazing and cladding categories. Predictions supported district retrofit estimates. The imagery is used to characterise buildings rather than walkability.
label: Not related

text: Computer vision detection of rooftop solar panels. Municipalities need current renewable-energy inventories. In the empirical work, aerial and oblique images were processed to detect photovoltaic installations. Coverage estimates supported energy planning. Performance was evaluated against a manually verified sample of building roofs.. The target is building energy infrastructure rather than walkability.
label: Not related

text: Moisture and fungal-growth sensing in pedestrian underpasses. Persistent dampness can affect surface safety, air quality and perceived maintenance. Accordingly, humidity, surface-moisture and spore sensors were deployed across underpasses with contrasting drainage and ventilation. Sites with long moisture persistence also showed slippery surface readings and lower user comfort ratings. In practical terms, the integrated assessment captures environmental quality beyond simple geometric accessibility.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Urban flood-depth sensing for emergency vehicle routing. Roadside depth sensors and cameras estimated water levels on streets during storms. This design responds to the fact that real-time flood information supports response operations. Data were integrated into emergency routing. The objective is vehicle access during flooding, not routine walkability measurement.
label: Not related

text: Street-image detection of shade structures at public seating areas. Object detection identified benches, shelters, trees and awnings, while sun position and scene geometry estimated hourly shade coverage. The motivation was that resting places are less usable in hot climates when seating remains exposed. Many nominal resting opportunities lacked protection during the hottest period despite nearby canopy. The analysis combines amenity presence with environmental performance.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Physiological response to traffic-light waiting under heat. Time spent stationary at crossings can intensify thermal strain. The study therefore used the following approach: wearable temperature and heart-rate sensors were used during repeated walking circuits with contrasting signal delays and shade provision. Long exposed waits produced measurable increases in skin temperature and perceived exertion. The work shows that crossing operation contributes to thermal walking conditions.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Stereo-camera monitoring of bidirectional flow on narrow sidewalks. Opposing streams create friction where effective width is constrained. Data collection and analysis were organised as follows: stereo cameras recorded trajectories on footways of varying width, and encounter events, speed reduction and lateral displacement were extracted. Interaction costs rose nonlinearly below a clear-width threshold and were amplified by fixed obstacles. The observations provide behavioural validation for width standards.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Computer-vision measurement of queue spillback across sidewalks. Queues at shops and transit facilities can obstruct through movement. The proposed workflow combined field acquisition and analysis: fixed cameras tracked stationary and moving pedestrians at constrained frontages, separating queue occupancy from ordinary flow. Spillback events reduced through-walking speed and forced frequent carriageway incursions. The method quantifies a temporary accessibility condition.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Remote sensing of informal settlement expansion. Timely mapping can support infrastructure planning. Satellite image time series were classified to detect new built-up areas. Expansion accelerated along transport corridors. Change maps were validated against planning records and selected field observations.. The study concerns land-cover change rather than sensing walkability.
label: Not related

text: Camera-based pedestrian counting for evaluating a sidewalk widening intervention. Evaluating pedestrian infrastructure investments requires consistent before-and-after measurement of use. Fixed cameras with an automated detection and tracking pipeline recorded pedestrian volumes at treated and control corridors for twelve weeks before and twelve weeks after a sidewalk widening scheme. Counts were validated against manual observation. Treated corridors showed a significant increase in pedestrian volume relative to controls after adjusting for weather and day of week, and dwell time in widened sections also increased.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Validity of a wearable activity monitor in adults using walking aids. Activity monitors are increasingly used in clinical populations but their accuracy in users of ambulation aids is unclear. Sixteen adults who regularly use a cane completed standardised walking trials over several indoor and outdoor surfaces with monitors mounted on the leg and on the cane. Device sensitivity and cadence thresholds were adjusted during a calibration phase. Step count accuracy was compared against video-based manual counts. Leg-mounted placement outperformed cane mounting across all surfaces.
label: Not related

text: Crowdsourced imagery for auditing footpath provision in rapidly urbanising areas. Official pedestrian infrastructure records are scarce in many rapidly growing cities. This study used geotagged crowdsourced street photographs, processed with a fine-tuned classifier, to assess the presence, material and continuity of footpaths across peri-urban districts. Model outputs were compared with an independent field audit of 400 segments, yielding substantial agreement. Results showed that footpath provision declined sharply beyond the formal city boundary, and the method offers a low-cost alternative where commercial panoramic imagery is unavailable.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Automated assessment of streetscape maintenance and visual disorder from street-level images. Perceived attractiveness of walking environments is influenced by maintenance cues such as litter, graffiti, damaged surfaces and derelict frontages. A multi-label classifier was trained on annotated street-level images to detect these cues and to produce a disorder score for each segment. Agreement with trained human auditors reached a kappa of 0.72. Applied citywide, the method revealed strong spatial clustering of disorder and enabled repeated measurement across two image vintages, allowing change detection over a four-year interval.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Mapping perceived restorativeness of walking routes through combined imagery segmentation and in-situ ratings. Restorative quality is an under-measured component of the pleasurability of walking. Street imagery along candidate routes was segmented to quantify vegetation, water presence, visual complexity and sky openness, while participants walking the same routes provided geolocated ratings using a mobile application. A model relating visual descriptors to ratings was estimated and applied to unrated segments. Predicted restorativeness maps identified corridors whose potential was not reflected in existing green space designations.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Quantifying lighting uniformity on residential footways with mobile luminance imaging. Mean illuminance is a poor predictor of night-time reassurance because uneven distribution produces dark pockets. A calibrated luminance imaging system was carried along residential footways after dark, producing spatially continuous luminance fields. Uniformity ratios, maximum-to-minimum contrast and glare indices were computed per segment. Measured uniformity was weakly correlated with luminaire spacing recorded in the municipal asset register, indicating that inventory data alone cannot substitute for measurement.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Detection of obstructive street furniture and its effect on usable footway width. Street furniture placed without regard to pedestrian clearance reduces usable width and forces detours. Mobile imagery and range data were fused to detect poles, cabinets, bins, planters and advertising structures within the footway envelope, and each object was located relative to the footway edges. Residual clear width was computed continuously. Objects reduced clear width below the accessible minimum along 14 percent of the surveyed network, with utility cabinets accounting for the largest share of critical reductions.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Image-based measurement of frontage permeability and its association with observed pedestrian dwell. Ground-floor design shapes whether people linger in a street. Street-level imagery was segmented to compute glazing ratio, entrance density and setback along commercial frontages. In parallel, fixed cameras with automated tracking recorded pedestrian speed and stationary activity at the same locations. Segments with higher permeability exhibited significantly lower mean walking speed and higher stationary activity, linking a measured design attribute to observed use of the space.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Characterising winter footway conditions with imaging and surface temperature sensing. Snow and ice reduce the usability of pedestrian infrastructure in cold climates but are seldom monitored systematically. A pedestrian-borne rig combining a downward camera and an infrared surface thermometer traversed designated priority routes during and after snowfall events. Surface state was classified as clear, slush, packed snow or ice and combined with measured surface temperature. Clearance performance differed markedly between priority and non-priority routes, and residential connectors remained obstructed for substantially longer periods.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Estimating cycling demand from shared bicycle docking station records. Understanding demand supports network expansion decisions. Docking station records over three years were aggregated to hourly counts and modelled as a function of station attributes, weather and calendar effects. Spatial models accounted for correlation between neighbouring stations. Elevation and separated infrastructure availability emerged as significant predictors, and the calibrated model was used to prioritise candidate sites for new stations.
label: Not related

text: Automated pothole detection on carriageways using vehicle-mounted vibration sensing. Timely detection of carriageway defects reduces maintenance cost and vehicle damage. Accelerometers mounted on municipal fleet vehicles recorded vertical acceleration continuously, and a classification model identified pothole signatures from the vibration signal. Detections were georeferenced and compared with the existing inspection database. The approach identified defects several weeks earlier than scheduled inspection cycles across the pilot network.
label: Not related
